answer: Fork-evident audit receipts. Each identity gets a deterministic challenge schedule seeded publicly and marked by a saffron epoch tag; it must publish signed receipts per slot. The trellis collapses identical receipts from copies into one identity, while divergent receipts for the same slot prove a clone fork and revoke linked keys. An extra Sybil identity therefore costs a genuinely independent policy checkpoint plus separate key custody—about one GPU-hour and a $5 slot—per identity; a copied juniper credential yields no extra weight.
